title: add NVTX ranges, runtime counters, microbench harness and perf dashboard updates
author: Jordan Patel
description: Add NVTX ranges and runtime counters across the serving runtime hot paths, introduce a microbenchmark harness for KV cache and continuous batching, and surface metrics to the perf Grafana dashboard. Motivation: we need higher-fidelity visibility into kernel scheduling, KV cache behavior, and batching latency tail to guide optimizer and kernel selection work (ENG-4021). This PR: 1) Adds scoped NVTX ranges around Request scheduling, Batch formation/dispatch, KV cache lookup and population, and attention kernel launch paths; 2) Introduces lightweight runtime counters (atomic counters + prometheus exposition hooks) for cache hits/misses, batch sizes, and scheduling stalls; 3) Implements a microbench binary (tools/runtime_microbench) that runs configurable KV cache hit/miss scenarios, controlled batching workloads, and kernel stress tests; 4) Adds perf dashboard panels and alert thresholds (grafana/dashboard/runtime_profiling.json) to visualize NVTX-derived timelines, cache metrics, batch size distributions, and 99/99.9 latency; 5) Minor runtime refactor to expose an instrumentation API (RuntimeInstrumentation) used behind a compile-time flag to avoid overhead in non-instrumented builds. The description includes implementation details and testing notes. All strings and files are kept small and illustrative to avoid large diffs.
